messages.subject: average dashline
parts: in the ggplot2 boxplot the median gets calculated, but how about mean.  what is the best way to add it?  I prefer ggplot2 to calculate it.  I know geom_vline or hline adds it if I bring the data in, but preference would be for R do it based on how my x axis is separated.  Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: average dashline
parts:
On Tue, Mar 4, 2014 at 10:53 PM, J H <renalcl...@gmail.com> wrote:
> in the ggplot2 boxplot the median gets calculated, but how about mean. what
> is the best way to add it? I prefer ggplot2 to calculate it. I know
> geom_vline or hline adds it if I bring the data in, but preference would be
> for R do it based on how my x axis is separated. Thanks.

You would need to write a new stat_* function that works as
stat_boxplot (i.e. outputs the same values in a data.frame, see
?stat_boxplot).

*But* this is probably a bad idea. Boxplots are not just defined by
their visual aspect, the fact that the central line is the median, the
whiskers extend to 1.5 * the interquartile range etc. all participate
in the definition of what a botplot is. So by making a non-standard
boxplot, you will be confusing your readers. I would advise you to
create a new, different looking plot altogether if you want to show
the mean instead of the median.
